items.title: Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre: le choléra gagne du terrain
items.description: Le choléra se propage rapidement en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre, où des flambées touchent désormais six pays et exposent des millions d’enfants à un risque croissant, alerte l’UNICEF. Les pluies saisonnières, les inondations, les déplacements de population et la transmission transfrontalière accélèrent la propagation de cette maladie pourtant évitable. La République démocratique du Congo (RDC), la République du Congo, le Nigéria, le Tchad, le Cameroun et la République centrafricaine sont confrontés à des flambées actives. Les enfants représentent une part importante des cas. En République centrafricaine, les moins de 10 ans comptent pour 44 % des cas signalés. Au Tchad, près des deux tiers des infections concernent des enfants de moins de 15 ans. Au Cameroun, l’âge médian des patients n’est que de 10 ans, souligne l' UNICEF dans un communiqué de presse. Le Nigéria connaît actuellement la plus importante flambée de la région, avec plus de 50.000 cas cumulés et 338 décès signalés depuis le 1er janvier 2026. La flambée est particulièrement importante dans l’État de Borno. En RDC, plus de 30.400 cas et près de 700 décès ont été recensés, soit le bilan le plus lourd parmi les pays touchés. Deux corridors de transmission La propagation se concentre notamment le long de deux grands corridors. Dans le bassin du lac Tchad, la même souche de Vibrio cholerae O1 Ogawa circule au Tchad, au Cameroun et au Nigéria. Dans le bassin du fleuve Congo, les épidémies touchent la RDC, la République du Congo et la Centrafrique. Dans ces deux zones, les inondations saisonnières augmentent fortement le risque de transmission en contaminant les sources d’eau, en endommageant les infrastructures sanitaires et en compliquant l’accès aux communautés vulnérables. «Cette flambée n’est plus confinée aux frontières. Elle se déplace le long des fleuves, des routes commerciales et des mouvements de population, mettant des millions d’enfants en danger», a déclaré Gilles Fagninou, directeur régional de l’UNICEF pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre. «Nous savons comment arrêter le choléra», a-t-il ajouté, appelant à davantage d’urgence, d’investissements et de solidarité régionale pour empêcher que davantage d’enfants ne meurent d’une maladie évitable. 15 millions de dollars supplémentaires Avec les autorités nationales et locales, l’UNICEF et ses partenaires renforcent l’accès à l’eau potable et à l’assainissement, la surveillance des maladies, l’approvisionnement en matériel médical et les campagnes de vaccination orale contre le choléra. L’agence travaille également avec l’Organisation mondiale de la Santé ( OMS ), les Centres africains de contrôle et de prévention des maladies (CDC Afrique) et les pays de la région pour améliorer la coordination transfrontalière le long des principaux axes de transmission. Mais l’UNICEF souligne que ces efforts doivent s’accompagner d’investissements durables dans l’eau, l’assainissement et l’hygiène afin de prévenir de nouvelles flambées. L’agence appelle ainsi à mobiliser 15 millions de dollars supplémentaires au cours des six prochains mois pour intensifier les opérations d’urgence et protéger les enfants les plus exposés. Source: ONU Info L’article Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre: le choléra gagne du terrain est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Super Coupe d'Europe : Déjà un trophée pour le Paris Saint-Germain (PSG)
items.description: Le Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) a confirmé son statut de roi au sommet de l'Europe en battant Aston Villa sur le score de 2-1, lors de la Supercoupe de l'UEFA, mercredi 12 août 2026. Le club français, vainqueur de la Ligue des champions, s'est imposé grâce à des buts de Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (20ᵉ) et de Désiré Doué (61ᵉ), ce dernier ayant été validé après intervention de la VAR. Brian Madjo avait égalisé à la 45ᵉ minute pour les Villans, vainqueurs de la Ligue Europa. Le club français a déjà parcouru quelques kilomètres avant le retour des grands rendez-vous. En battant Aston Villa 2-1, Luis Enrique et ses hommes lancent parfaitement la nouvelle saison. Au terme d'un match palpitant, le club de la capitale française peut rêver d'un nouveau succès en Europe. D'une compétition continentale à une autre, le PSG poursuit sa domination. Vainqueur des deux dernières éditions de la Ligue des champions, le club français s'avançait naturellement comme le grand favori de cette rencontre face aux Anglais, vainqueurs de la Ligue Europa. Et ce, avec un groupe qui n'était pas encore au point physiquement, le match se jouant un mois après la Coupe du monde. On constate ce manque de préparation chez les joueurs des deux blocs : manque de précision, manque d'intensité dans les duels et fatigue. Les deux équipes ont parfois eu des difficultés à se frayer des chemins. Mais malgré cela, les Parisiens trouvent la bonne formule, car ils ont eu les occasions et n'ont pas hésité. La confiance d'un champion, sans doute. Après une vingtaine de minutes de jeu, remplies d'émotion, les hommes de Luis Enrique peinaient dans la construction. Ils trouvent toutefois la faille et ouvrent le score sur une superbe frappe de l'ailier géorgien Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. Alors que les Français contrôlaient le match, les joueurs d'Unai Emery s'organisent pour revenir rapidement au score, obtenant une série d'occasions par Brian Madjo. Titularisé à la pointe de l'attaque anglaise, le jeune buteur de 17 ans ne laisse pas la défense française respirer. Il parvient à éliminer William Pacho et inscrit le but égalisateur de la tête à la 45ᵉ minute, à la réception d'un centre millimétré de John McGinn. L'égalisation des Anglais galvanise davantage les Français et rend le match encore plus incertain. Lancé parfaitement en profondeur par son coéquipier, Désiré Doué prend le temps nécessaire pour redonner l'avantage aux Parisiens. Le drapeau du hors-jeu se lève, puis la VAR intervient pour finalement valider le but. Luis Enrique et ses hommes verrouillent tout et ne laissent plus filer leur avantage. Le PSG peut rêver d'un deuxième trophée de la saison, dimanche prochain à Lens, à l'occasion du Trophée des champions. Ismaël Ouédraogo (stagiaire) Lefaso.net

items.title: Pakistan, Norway reaffirm resolve to strengthen bilateral ties, expand engagement in defence and security
items.description: Pakistan and Norway on Thursday reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation in defence and security. Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide, who is on a two-day visit to Pakistan, called on Chief of Defence Forces and the Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, with the two leaders reiterating their resolve to further strengthen bilateral ties and expand engagement in defence and security, according to a statement issued by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR). The two sides discussed matters of “mutual interest, regional security, and bilateral relations”. During the meeting, Field Marshal Munir highlighted “Pakistan’s perspective on global peace and regional stability” and stressed the “importance of cooperation and collaborative efforts to address common security challenges”. The Norwegian foreign minister appreciated the “professional role” played by the Pakistan Armed Forces “in promoting regional peace and stability”. Earlier in the day, Eide addressed a press conference alongside Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad, during which he lauded Pakistan’s mediatory role in the US-Iran conflict, saying it was a “service to the world and hence, also to us”. “I also really want to reiterate our strong support for the very important role that Pakistan has taken in this dramatic war that started on February 28 with the US-Israel attack on Iran,” he said, recalling that Norway was one of the Western countries that was “clearest and earliest” in stating that the war was a violation of international rules. “If we stand up for international law, it has to apply to everyone, everywhere, all the time,” he stressed. He said that while Norway had “significant disagreements with Iran on other issues, they also have the right to be protected as a state”. Referring to Pakistan’s mediatory role in the ongoing conflict, he said he realised how difficult mediation and facilitation of parleys between the two sides could be. “I know what a massive task you were taking on when you offered Islamabad not only as the venue but also as the facilitator of these talks,” he said, lauding Pakistan’s civilian and military leadership for their efforts. “What you have been doing is really a service to the world, and hence, also to us.” The Norwegian diplomat said Pakistan’s mediation efforts also mattered to his country as it was a large shipping nation. “We share an interest in open sea lanes and the ability to trade in the high seas, and to respect the Constitution of the Oceans […] Whatever emerges from this tragic and unnecessary war in Gulf, we need to protect the principle of the free passage,” he explained. “And I am so happy we see completely eye to eye [on this],” he remarked. The visiting minister added that his message to “anyone involved out there in the conflict is that this issue of free passage and an open strait is not an issue for the warring parties alone. It is a global issue that we have a shared interest in promoting”. He said he had discussed other regional issues during the visit as well, ranging from the Kashmir issue to Afghanistan. Moreover, Eide said, he was glad to learn more about a recently signed defence pact between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia in Makkah. “These are three countries with whom Norway has very good and close relations,” he noted. At the outset of his address, Eide said he was honoured to be in Pakistan, saying the last time a Norwegian foreign minister visited Pakistan was 10 years ago. “So it was about time,” he remarked. “I promised you many months ago that I would come, and today, I live up to my promise. I was looking forward to this visit, which is short but very effective.” Eide said there was a “strong partnership” between Norway and Pakistan, as well as the people of the two countries. “We have a sizeable diaspora of Pakistani descent […] Many of them are in key positions of politics and society and are a very welcome contribution to our country; and the fact that we have so many people who know these two countries intimately is yet another argument for strengthening our economic ties,” he added. The Norwegian foreign minister further said that Oslo and Islamabad were discussing strengthening economic ties “in the context of specifics” and enhancing trade ties in more structural ways. He also mentioned climate change and floods in Pakistan, saying that the two sides agreed it was a foreign policy issue. “And if you need one additional argument for stopping wars apart from relieving suffering and ending economic harm, it is that mankind should collectively try to focus on the real issues that require real cooperative action,” he said. Eide said combating nature loss and climate change, promoting global health and fighting poverty were among the issues on his agenda for discussions during the visit. Speaking earlier, Dar said the two countries had agreed to enhance bilateral ties and cooperation in all areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, education, defence, climate change, information technology and maritime affairs. He said Pakistan greatly valued its relations with Norway and looked forward to further strengthening them in the days, weeks and months ahead. Dar also said bilateral political consultations (BPC) between the two countries had become a regular feature of their engagement. “We are looking forward to hosting the next round of BPC in Islamabad later this year in the winter,” he said. Dar said the two sides also agreed that bilateral trade between Norway and Pakistan was “below the potential of both economies and needs to be enhanced through effective measures”. “Pakistan offers enormous investment opportunities to Norwegian companies, and it is heartening to see many leading Norwegian companies investing in Pakistan. “A renowned Norwegian company, Yara International, is establishing a joint venture in plant nutrition with the Fauji Fertiliser company. I hope this initiative will be a trailblazer for many more future projects between our two great countries,” he added. Dar termed Pakistan’s partnership with Norway in the field of technology “a success story”. “Pakistan’s IT exports to Norway have grown more than five-fold in the last two years, and I have no doubt that this is only the beginning.” He further stated that the two sides also agreed on the expedient finalisation of various agreements and memoranda of understanding (MoU). On climate change, he said there was a convergence of perspectives between the two countries. “It is heartening to note that Pakistan and Norway signed the MoU under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on April 1 this year,” he said, adding that the two sides also held talks on cooperation in maritime affairs. He said he had told the visiting dignitary that Pakistan was “one of the world’s largest ship recycling facilities, and our strategic location makes it the most competitive and nearest recycling destination in this maritime region for ships coming from Norway”. Dar thanked Norway’s maritime authorities for their support in capacity building and providing technical training for Pakistan’s shipbreaking industry in line with the Hong Kong International Convention. He added that Pakistan and Norway had agreed to enhance people-to-people contact, which he said could become “defining for our relations and serve as social and cultural bridges between the two countries”. The DPM said the two sides had also discussed labour mobility. “We agreed to continue work on legal pathways for Pakistan’s skilled manpower, expressing the need to combat human smuggling and illegal migration. Both sides agreed that by providing safe, orderly and regular migration channels, we not only protect migrants’ rights and lives but also dismantle the illegal model of smuggling networks,” he elaborated. Dar further said that both Pakistan and Norway shared a commitment to multilateralism, the principles of the United Nations Charter, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity and the peaceful settlement of disputes. “Our two countries remain actively engaged on issues related to the UN Security Council, and the two sides have strong convergence of views on major issues. “Building on our previous experience of working together in international bodies and multilateral fora, both sides affirm their desire to continue mutual support and consultations on such forums.” Dar said he had also briefed the Norwegian foreign minister and delegation on the Kashmir issue. He said he told them that India had added a new dimension to an already volatile security situation by unilaterally announcing the abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty in contravention of international law. “We reiterate that India must end the weaponisation of water and uphold its treaty obligations under international legal obligations,” he asserted. Dar said he had further briefed the Norwegian foreign minister on Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts for promoting dialogue, de-escalation and peaceful settlement of the US-Iran conflict. He thanked him for appreciating Pakistan’s role as a mediator in the conflict. Moreover, he said, he had broadly discussed the Makkah defence pact with the visiting dignitary. “We had a great discussion, and it happens that all three countries enjoy the best of relations with Norway,” he said. The DPM concluded his address, saying: “We agreed on the need to find peaceful solutions to the international conflicts in full respect of the principles of international law and the UN Charter. “I thank his excellency, my dear friend, for his visit. I am confident that this visit will open a new chapter in Pakistan-Norway relations and will contribute to greater cooperation and mutual prosperity for the people of both countries in the years ahead.” Delegation-level talks Earlier in the day, Eide held delegation-level talks with DPM Dar, according to the Foreign Office (FO). During the talks, the two sides reviewed the whole gamut of bilateral cooperation in various fields, including trade, investment, climate change, maritime affairs and education. They recognised the important role of the Pakistani diaspora in Norway and agreed to strengthen people-to-people ties between the two countries. The two sides expressed satisfaction at the warm and cordial state of Pakistan-Norway relations and agreed to further deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest,” it said. FO said the two sides also held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments of mutual interest. During the delegation-level talks, the visiting dignitary also recognised Pakistan’s role in the US-Iran war as “important and constructive”, lauding the leadership of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal Munir and DPM Dar, as per the FO statement. Eide had also appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to promote peace and expressed Norway’s desire to further strengthen bilateral ties earlier in the day in televised remarks. He said Norway and Pakistan had a “very strong bilateral partnership”, adding that the presence of a large Pakistani community in Norway, which was “well integrated into Norwegian society”, had helped strengthen ties between the two countries. “There are many leading politicians in Norway and many close colleagues who are actually of Pakistani-Norwegian descent, so it has really made a mark,” he said. Eide said business ties between the two countries were also growing, particularly in the energy and fertiliser sectors, with Norwegian companies increasingly looking at opportunities in Pakistan. He said Norway also saw opportunities for Pakistan to strengthen economic relations through its cooperation with Switzerland and Iceland, noting that the three countries could provide further avenues for expanding business relations. Turning to the regional situation, Eide strongly commended the actions taken by Pakistan’s leadership. Eide described the ongoing war as “incredibly dangerous” for global peace as well as the world economy, and praised Pakistan for stepping forward. He also appreciated Pakistan’s role in facilitating the Islamabad talks and maintaining engagement with the parties involved. “I think it is fair to say that the position of Pakistan on the world stage, also in peacemaking, has really been strengthened by this commitment,” he said. Eide said Norway was ready to assist Pakistan’s peace efforts, noting that Oslo had experience in peace negotiations and maintained open dialogue with both Tehran and Washington. “Wherever we can be useful, we will,” he said. He also highlighted Norway’s experience in international maritime affairs, saying the country was among the world’s major seafaring nations despite its relatively small population. He said Norway could therefore play a constructive role in discussions concerning international maritime law and developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz. Dar, Eide discuss bilateral ties The two ministers also held a “restricted-format meeting” earlier today, FO said. “DPM Dar warmly welcomed Eide to Pakistan. The two ministers discussed the full range of bilateral relations, as well as regional and international developments, and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation in all areas of mutual interest,” according to FO. Upon his arrival in Islamabad, Eide was received at the airport by Additional Foreign Secretary (Europe) Ambassador Ayesha Ali. In a statement on Wednesday, the FO said the minister is undertaking the visit from Aug 13-14 at Dar’s invitation. The visit is the first by a Norwegian foreign minister in a decade, the FO said, adding that the visit would build on high-level engagement between the two countries, including phone conversation between Dar and Eide in March and April , and the visit of Norway’s State Secretary Andreas Motzfeldt Kravik to Islamabad in May. The FO stated that the visit would provide an opportunity to “further strengthen the longstanding and cordial relations between Pakistan and Norway and to explore new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation”.

items.title: Upper West records 45% drop in maternal deaths ahead of free primary healthcare rollout
items.description: The Upper West Region has recorded a nearly 45% reduction in maternal deaths and is now counting down to the rollout of Free Primary Healthcare in 10 municipalities and districts, covering about 790,000 people. Health authorities say the policy has the potential to transform healthcare delivery, but only if all stakeholders work together to ensure that “no one is left behind”. Speaking at the Mid-Year Health Sector Review, the Upper West Regional Director of Health Services, Dr Josephat Nyuzagl, announced that the region’s maternal mortality ratio had dropped from 87.82 to 48.5 per 100,000 live births, representing a 45% reduction. “I’m particularly pleased to report a decline in anaemia among pregnant women. We also recorded an increase in skilled deliveries,” Dr Nyuzagl said, reaffirming the region’s efforts to ensure that more women deliver safely. He added that healthcare utilisation had increased, while civil works for the regional oxygen plant had been completed. Equipment installation is expected to be completed within eight weeks. Dr Nyuzagl said the region was prepared for the Free Primary Healthcare policy launched by President John Mahama in April 2026. Phase One of the policy covers 10 of the region’s 11 municipalities and districts, accounting for about 78% of the Upper West Region’s population. To prepare for the rollout, the region has received 853 pieces of equipment across 72 categories and has interviewed 199 health workers for deployment. “Free primary healthcare is not charity. This is an investment in equity, an investment in human capital,” he stated. Despite the progress, Dr Nyuzagl identified infrastructure and accommodation challenges that could affect the delivery of primary healthcare. “A number of CHPS zones lack CHPS compounds. If we want community health officers to be closer to communities, it’s important that they have accommodation,” he said. He also announced new Ghana Health Service directives, including the installation of CCTV cameras in all health facilities, mandatory staff identification cards and stronger safety measures. Speaking on behalf of the Upper West Regional Minister, Charles Lwanga Puozuing, Chief Director Pognaa Fati Issaka Koray said the Free Primary Healthcare policy had “the potential to transform healthcare delivery and improve the lives of our people”. “Today’s gathering serves two important purposes. First, to reflect on our performance. Second, to embrace a policy that can transform healthcare delivery,” she said. She called on Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) to prioritise healthcare in their budgets and urged traditional and religious leaders to support health education within their communities. “The success of this policy will depend on all of us. Investment in primary healthcare is an investment in human development and sustainable growth,” she stated. On the challenges facing maternal and child health, she was emphatic. “Every preventable maternal or neonatal death is one too many. Our goal must remain clear to ensure that every woman, every child, and every family has access to quality and timely healthcare services,” she said. She also stressed that the Free Primary Healthcare programme must place greater emphasis on disease prevention. “Preventing illness is often more effective and less costly than treating advanced disease,” she added. With equipment delivered, health workers recruited and the implementation roadmap circulated, health officials say the Upper West Region is “done and ready for a smooth take-off”.

items.title: Ouaga | Braquages de clients de banques : Le Tribunal renvoie le dossier pour examiner les caméras de surveillance
items.description: Pendant cinq jours, le tribunal spécialisé dans les infractions économiques et la criminalité organisée a planché sur 13 dossiers. Au final, 9 prévenus ont été jugés, écopant de peines de prison et d’amendes pour blanchiment, escroquerie ou abus de biens sociaux. Une affaire de braquages sanglants, elle, a été renvoyée pour expertise. Le pôle judiciaire ECOFI (infractions économiques, financières et criminalité organisée) du Tribunal de grande instance Ouaga I a tenu sa session de rentrée judiciaire du 3 au 7 août 2026. Sur les 13 dossiers inscrits au rôle, 7 ont été effectivement jugés, impliquant 9 prévenus. Les faits poursuivis couvrent un large spectre : blanchiment de capitaux, abus de biens sociaux, escroquerie, faux en écriture publique et privée, fraude sur la commercialisation de l’or, et même meurtre. Pour les coupables reconnus, le tribunal a systématiquement assorti les peines privatives de liberté d’amendes fermes. L’affaire la plus emblématique de cette session concerne une série de braquages à main armée qui ont secoué Ouagadougou au second semestre 2025. Les cibles sont des clients de banques venant d’effectuer des retraits importants. Les suspects, poursuivis pour grand banditisme, meurtre et blanchiment, ont vu leur dossier renvoyé après deux jours de débat. Le tribunal a ordonné une expertise des images de vidéosurveillance pour éclairer sa décision. Dans son communiqué, le Procureur du Faso a salué la résilience des acteurs de la chaîne pénale, qui ont permis la tenue de cette session malgré des moyens limités et un effectif réduit en raison des vacances judiciaires. items.title: One dead, 14 injured in Bunso Highway crash
items.description: One person has died, and 14 others have been injured after a MAN Diesel truck and a Toyota Hiace collided on the Accra–Kumasi Highway near Paradise Restaurant at Bunso in the Eastern Region. This was made known in a statement issued by the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) Public Relations Officer (PRO) for the Eastern Region on Thursday, August 13. According to the report, the crash occurred after the MAN Diesel truck reportedly veered into the opposite lane while attempting to give way to a Toyota Vitz. The truck subsequently collided with the Toyota Hiace, resulting in the death of one person and injuries to 14 others. The GNFS from the Bunso Fire Station were called to the scene and carried out the rescue operation. They also helped retrieve personal belongings from the vehicles and cleared the crash site to allow traffic to resume. The report did not provide details about the identities of the deceased and injured persons or the extent of their injuries. The circumstances leading to the crash are expected to be investigated by the relevant authorities.

items.title: Al Ahly : Coup d’arrêt pour Youssef Belammari, victime d’une rupture du ligament croisé
items.description: Le défenseur marocain Youssef Belammari, joueur d’Al Ahly d’Égypte, a été victime d’une rupture du ligament croisé du genou. Une blessure sérieuse qui devrait l’éloigner des terrains pendant une longue période. Mauvaise nouvelle pour Youssef Belammari. Le latéral gauche marocain d’Al Ahly s’est gravement blessé lors du stage de préparation du club égyptien en Espagne, à quelques semaines du début de la nouvelle saison. Après avoir passé des examens médicaux ainsi qu’une IRM du genou, le verdict est tombé : le joueur souffre d’une rupture du ligament croisé. L’information a été confirmée par Ahmed Gaballah, responsable du staff médical de l’équipe première d’Al Ahly, dans une déclaration publiée par le service communication du club. Le staff médical d’Al Ahly travaille désormais sur la programmation de l’intervention chirurgicale que devra subir le défenseur marocain. « Les examens et l’imagerie par résonance magnétique ont confirmé sa blessure au ligament croisé du genou », a indiqué Ahmed Gaballah. Le club doit déterminer dans les prochains jours la date de l’opération. Après son intervention, Belammari entamera un long programme de soins et de rééducation, indispensable avant d’envisager un retour à la compétition. Cette blessure intervient alors qu’Al Ahly se trouve actuellement en Espagne pour préparer la prochaine saison. Youssef Belammari devait profiter de cette période pour monter progressivement en puissance et se préparer aux prochaines échéances avec son club. Sa blessure vient donc brutalement interrompre sa préparation. Une rupture du ligament croisé représente généralement une absence de plusieurs mois, même si la durée exacte de l’indisponibilité dépendra de l’évolution de son état et de sa rééducation. Pour l’instant, Al Ahly n’a pas communiqué de durée précise d’indisponibilité. Le joueur devra d’abord passer par la case opération, avant de débuter un long parcours de rééducation. items.title: Man City reject £55m Barcelona offer for Rodri
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Manchester City have rejected a £55m bid from Barcelona for midfielder Rodri, with the Spanish club still keen to sign the World Cup-winning midfielder. Barcelona had previously seen an offer of around £40m rejected by City before returning with an improved proposal. However, the latest bid has also been turned down, with City reportedly seeking more than £60m for the 30-year-old. Despite the latest setback, Barcelona remain interested in Rodri and are considering their next move as negotiations continue. Rodri has entered the final year of his contract at the Etihad, but City are reluctant to sell the Spain international and would prefer to extend his deal. According to Sky Sports, City do not want to lose the midfielder and hope to reach an agreement over a new contract. However, the club would not stand in his way if Rodri formally asks to leave. The main point of disagreement between the two clubs is their valuation of the midfielder. Manchester City are demanding an initial guaranteed fee of between €70m and €80m before considering Rodri’s departure. Barcelona, however, are constrained by La Liga’s financial fair-play rules and can currently offer a package capped at around €65m. Much of the Spanish club’s proposal is tied to variables, add-ons and other conditional payments rather than an immediate guaranteed fee. City could therefore lose two central midfielders this summer, although the club are also exploring replacements, including Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez and Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi. The post Man City reject £55m Barcelona offer for Rodri appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Prioritise party interest over individual interests – NPP tells aspirants
items.description: The Chairperson of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) National Elections Committee, Frederick Opare-Ansah, has urged aspirants and delegates participating in the party’s upcoming national executive elections to put the interests of the party above their personal ambitions. Opare-Ansah said the success of the NPP should remain the primary consideration for all stakeholders as the party prepares to elect its national leadership ahead of the 2028 general elections. He made the call at a press conference in Accra on Thursday, August 13th, 2026, as the party intensifies preparations for its national delegates conference. He cautioned aspirants and delegates against actions or statements that could undermine the party’s unity and cohesion during and after the elections. According to him, while it was legitimate for aspirants to pursue their individual ambitions, those ambitions should not take precedence over the broader interests of the NPP. “Know the rules, respect the rules, use the established processes and put the interest of the party above individual interests,” he said. He further appealed to all participants to respect the rules and regulations governing the electoral process and allow the committee to discharge its mandate fairly and transparently. Mr Opare-Ansah assured stakeholders that the National Elections Committee would give a listening ear to all concerns and ensure that matters brought before it were handled fairly. He said the committee was committed to creating a level playing field for all aspirants and ensuring that the electoral process was conducted in a manner that would strengthen the party. “We will be impartial, we will be transparent, we will apply the rules fairly and firmly. We will provide the opportunity for legitimate grievances to be heard throughout the process. We will work to deliver an election whose outcome will reflect the freely expressed choice of the delegates,” he said. The upcoming national delegates conference is expected to elect new national executives who will lead the NPP as it reorganises and positions itself for the 2028 general elections. Mr Opare-Ansah therefore called on all aspirants and delegates to conduct themselves responsibly and place the unity and future of the party above individual interests.

items.title: Sourou : Les ressortissants de Toarè offrent 619 500 F CFA de soutien aux VDP de Tougan
items.description: BURKINA-SOUROU-DON-VDP Sourou : Les ressortissants de Toarè offrent 619 500 F CFA de soutien aux VDP de Tougan Tougan, 13 août 2026 (AIB) – Les ressortissants du village de Toarè ont contribué à l’effort de reconquête du territoire national en remettant, mercredi, aux Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP) de Tougan, un don composé de vivres et d’une enveloppe financière, d’une valeur totale de 619 500 F CFA. La cérémonie de remise s’est tenue dans les locaux de la Police municipale de Tougan, en présence du président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune, Ouigou Tiendrebéogo. Le don est constitué de 30 sacs de riz de 25 kg, de six cartons de spaghetti, de trois bidons d’huile de 20 litres et d’une somme de 150 000 F CFA en espèces. Selon le porte-parole des donateurs, Mahamoudou Zerbo, cette contribution vise à soutenir les efforts de reconquête du territoire engagés par les forces combattantes. « Les gens font des sacrifices énormes pour pacifier la zone. Il est donc bon et bienséant de porter une contribution à l’effort qu’ils mènent sur le terrain », a-t-il déclaré. M. Zerbo a invité l’ensemble des populations à ne ménager aucun effort pour apporter leur contribution à l’effort de paix et de reconquête du territoire, quelle qu’en soit la nature. Le coordonnateur des VDP communaux de Tougan, le sergent Soumaïla Bamogo, a, au nom de sa hiérarchie, exprimé sa reconnaissance aux donateurs. « Nous sommes très contents d’avoir reçu ce don ce matin. C’est un don qui va nous galvaniser dans la lutte que nous menons. Nous remercions les donateurs », a-t-il affirmé. À son tour, le PDS de Tougan, Ouigou Tiendrebéogo, a salué la solidarité des ressortissants de Toarè et les a remerciés pour leur geste, qu’il a qualifié de « hautement patriotique ». Il a estimé que cette contribution permettra de galvaniser et de motiver davantage les VDP sur le terrain, tout en témoignant de la solidarité et du soutien de la population à leur égard. Agence d’information du Burkina SS/no/yos

items.title: Pakistan's first lunar rover named 'Jinnah-1': Suparco
items.description: Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) on Thursday announced “Jinnah-1” as the official name of the country’s first lunar rover. The rover is scheduled to be sent to the Moon in 2029 as part of China’s Chang’e-8 mission, where it will conduct scientific research at the lunar south pole, Suparco said. The Moon’s south pole is known for its challenging terrain and potential to yield significant scientific discoveries. In a ceremony held in Islamabad, Suparco said that the name was selected from 4,000 proposals received in a countrywide competition. Seven participants had proposed the name “Jinnah-1” and the winner was selected through a lucky draw, according to a statement from Suparco. Tayyab Karim, a 17-year-old from Bahawalnagar, was declared the winner for proposing the name, Suparco said. The name pays tribute to Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah and symbolises “Pakistan’s resolve, progress and new space horizons”, Suparco Chairman said. Jinnah-1 will study plasma, radiation and the lunar surface’s geology, as well as conduct key experiments related to future lunar research and the prospect of human presence on the Moon, Suparco said. Pakistan’s first lunar rover, Jinnah-1, will be a part of China’s Chang’e-8 mission to the Moon’s south pole in 2029. —Photo courtesy of Suparco Suparco announced the collaboration with China’s Chang’e-8 mission in 2024. “This collaboration marks a significant milestone for Pakistan’s space programme, as Suparco’s indigenous rover will be part of the mission to explore the lunar surface,” the space agency said at the time. Nasa is targeting 2028 for the first-ever landing of astronauts on the Moon’s south pole, as part of Artemis IV, seeking to beat China’s planned crewed mission, Chang’e-8, to the same lunar region. In 2023, India managed to land a craft — the unmanned Chandrayaan-3 — near the Moon’s south pole. Its landing came days after a Russian probe crashed in the same region and four years since the previous Indian attempt failed at the last moment.

items.title: Nigeria take on South Africa in World Cup playoff today – time and where to watch
items.description: African women’s football giants South Africa and Nigeria clash on Thursday in Casablanca under high-pressure circumstances neither team envisioned. Following shocking quarter-final exits at the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), one of the continent’s last two champions will see their 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup qualification hopes officially vanish. South Africa’s Banyana Banyana fell 2–1 to host nation Morocco in the last eight, while Nigeria’s Super Falcons suffered a narrow 1–0 defeat to Cameroon. With the winners of those quarter-final ties securing automatic spots for the World Cup in Brazil, the two heavyweight losers are now forced to fight through the play-off route. The Long Road to Brazil 2027 A victory on Thursday keeps a faint World Cup dream alive, but the path ahead remains steep. The winner will advance to a six-team preliminary round in the Inter-Confederation play-offs. From there, two teams will progress to a final play-off phase alongside four nations that receive direct byes. Ultimately, three teams from the final six-nation tournament will lock in their tickets to Brazil via single-elimination knockout matches. In practical terms, Thursday’s clash in Morocco is just the first of three distinct hurdles—including a mini-tournament and two must-win knockout fixtures; standing between either nation and a spot at the global showpiece. While both camps are devastated to miss out on direct qualification, the door to Brazil is not completely shut just yet. Match Details Date: Thursday, August 13 Time: 9:00 p.m. WAT Venue: Stade Moulay Rachid, Casablanca, Morocco How to Watch: Live on AfroSport (Nigeria), SABC (South Africa), and SuperSport across the region. items.title: Abductors of Anambra billionaire businessman, Jezco, demand N1.5bn ransom
items.description: The abductors of the Chairman of Jezco Group, Chief Sir Joseph Ezeokafor, have reportedly increased their ransom demand to N1.5 billion, according to a report by Arise TV. Ezeokafor, a septuagenarian businessman, was reportedly abducted in the early hours of Tuesday while on his way to a prayer ground for his annual spiritual rejuvenation. A source close to the family, who spoke on condition of anonymity, told Arise TV that the kidnappers initially demanded N700 million for the businessman’s release. The family was reportedly prepared to negotiate the payment in a bid to secure his freedom. However, the abductors were said to have subsequently raised their demand to N1.5 billion. The source further disclosed that communication between the kidnappers and the family had since broken down, despite the family’s reported willingness to continue negotiations. The development has reportedly left the businessman’s relatives in a difficult situation as attempts to re-establish contact with the abductors have so far been unsuccessful. Ezeokafor was said to have left his home at about 2am without his security details, reportedly making him vulnerable to the abductors. The incident has generated concern among his associates and members of his community. However, neither the Anambra State Police Command nor the state government has publicly commented on the reported abduction of the businessman, about a week after the incident. The circumstances surrounding his whereabouts and the current efforts to secure his release remain unclear. The post Abductors of Anambra billionaire businessman, Jezco, demand N1.5bn ransom appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Connexion mobile | La Tunisie 3e parmi 7 pays à richesse par habitant comparable
items.description: Selon les données collectées par nPerf , une plateforme indépendante de mesure des performances Internet, basée sur l'expérience réelle des utilisateurs, la Tunisie se classe 3 e des connexions mobiles, avec 56 696 nPoints, parmi 7 pays à richesse par habitant comparable (entre 3000 et 5000 US $), entre janvier et juillet 2026. Ce score moyen reflète la performance globale des usages comme le téléchargement de fichiers, l’envoi de contenus ou la navigation web. Le Maroc et le Vietnam, avec respectivement 77 129 nPoints et 75 246 nPoints, devancent la Tunisie dans ce classement. La Tunisie précède cependant l’Égypte (33 090 nPoints), le Venezuela (29 993 nPoints), l’Angola (22 527 nPoints) et le Sri Lanka (16 752 nPoints). Les performances varient significativement parmi les pays à richesse par habitant comparable. Le Maroc, en tête, affiche un score supérieur de 20 433 nPoints à celui de la Tunisie. À l’inverse, la Tunisie dépasse le Sri Lanka de 39 944 nPoints, illustrant des différences notables dans l’expérience utilisateur, notamment pour des usages comme le téléchargement de vidéos en haute définition ou la navigation web fluide. items.description: By Caleb Ayemere The Lagos State government has vowed to intensify enforcement against individuals harassing motorists and stopping luxury vehicles along the Lekki Epe Expressway, describing the disruptive actions as strictly criminal. Speaking in a broadcast on Nigeria Info FM, Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat declared the state administration will take decisive, ongoing action to clear the major transit corridor of unauthorized individuals targeting high-end cars and compromising public safety. Hamzat condemned the activity, emphasizing that the government would not tolerate extortion or harassment on state roads and confirming that law enforcement agencies have already begun removing offenders from the axis. “That is criminal, and therefore, we will not allow it. So, we will take a lot of them off the street,” Hamzat stated. “A lot of people have been arrested, really. A lot of cameras are also on that road and people have been seen… some people are in the Magistrate Court today.” The deputy governor further revealed that security agencies have leveraged the state’s network of surveillance cameras along the Lekki Epe route to track down suspects, noting that multiple arrests were executed over the weekend as legal proceedings get underway. La session de formation a été initiée par l’Organisation des nations Unies pour l’alimentation et l’agriculture (FAO) en collaboration avec le ministère en charge de l’Agriculture, et l’Institut national de la propriété industrielle et de la technologie (INPIT). Elle entre dans la mise en œuvre du projet « Appui à la promotion de l’entrepreneuriat agricole des jeunes au Togo ». Les jeunes entrepreneurs et les responsables des structures d’accompagnement ont été éclairés sur la protection de leurs inventions, marques, savoir-faire et autres créations. Ils ont pris connaissance des fondamentaux de la propriété intellectuelle et des missions de l’OAPI/INPIT ; de la protection des inventions par brevet et l’utilisation stratégique des marques. Les participants ont été également édifiés sur la protection des secrets d’affaires et la valorisation des produits locaux à travers les marques collectives et les indications géographiques, ainsi que l’intégration de la propriété intellectuelle, comme outil de compétitivité des entreprises. Des jeunes entrepreneurs en salle Le chargé de programme à la FAO-Togo, Djiwa Oyétoundé, a relevé l’importance de la protection des idées et innovations pour accroître la valeur des produits agricoles et agroalimentaires. Selon lui, l’enjeu est désormais de produire mieux, transformer davantage les produits sur place, protéger les innovations et améliorer la commercialisation des produits togolais. Il a rappelé que dans le cadre ce projet, 164 plans d’affaires de jeunes ont été reçus par la FAO, dont 27 présélectionnés qui ont fait objet de missions d’approfondissement et d’échanges. M. Djiwa a exhorté ces jeunes entrepreneurs à considérer leurs productions non seulement comme des biens à commercialiser, mais aussi comme des marques, des savoir-faire et des innovations susceptibles de créer davantage de valeur. Le directeur régional de l’Agriculture de la Kara, Dadja Badalake, a déclaré que cette formation vient aider les entrepreneurs à donner davantage de valeur à leurs créations et à mieux protéger leurs innovations. « L’initiative prise aujourd’hui par la FAO vient amorcer un grand début pour le développement de notre agriculture », a-t-il renchéri. Il a convié les bénéficiaires à mettre en pratique les acquis en innovant dans d’autres domaines susceptibles de contribuer au développement durable. Des études de cas, travaux de groupe, simulations, échanges d’expériences et séances de questions-réponses ont marqué ces jours de formation. ATOP/AE/TAL/BV

Será la primera vez que la ciudad turca acoja el torneo, en el que participarán el actual campeón, el Real Madrid, el Atlético y la Real Sociedad y que se celebrará del 2 al 7 de febrero de 2027. items.title: High-profile terrorist commander killed in Bannu IBO: DPO
items.description: PESHAWAR: A highly wanted terrorist commander was killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) conducted by the Bannu police and the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD), the district police confirmed on Thursday. Bannu’s District Police Officer (DPO) Captain (retd) Muhammad Furqan Bilal confirmed the terrorist’s killing in a conversation with Dawn . The DPO confirmed that the terrorist was identified as a high-profile commander, Naseer Muhammad alias Geedarh , who carried a Rs6 million bounty on his head. According to a statement issued by the police, an operation is underway against terrorists in the jurisdiction of Domel Police Station under the supervision of DPO Bilal, involving both the Bannu district police and CTD teams. The statement elaborated that the operation is being conducted in Akbar Ali Khan Kili, Sada Khel, Sadarwan and the adjoining areas, where police and CTD teams are carrying out targeted actions based on intelligence reports regarding the presence and movement of terrorists. Search and surveillance operations are also underway in the area, while security has been further tightened in various parts of the Bannu township and Domel. The police said further details of the operation and its progress would be shared after the ongoing operation was completed. There has been a resurgence in terrorism in Pakistan since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in Kabul in 2021. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded. On Monday, the district police, CTD and security forces conducted a joint IBO in the jurisdiction of the Miryan police station in Bannu, leading to the killing of an unidentified terrorist in an exchange of fire and the arrest of 10 suspected individuals. Last week, a captain was martyred while seven terrorists were killed during an IBO in KP’s Hangu district. Separately, security forces killed a key terrorist commander identified as Jamidullah during an operation in Jani Khel area of Bannu, a security official said. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies , an Islamabad-based think tank, violence linked to terrorist attacks and counter-terrorism operations intensified sharply in July, making it the deadliest month of 2026, with 112 security personnel among 205 people killed.

items.title: Burkina: 60 millions FCFA de faux billets, 5kg de drogue et autres marchandises saisis
items.description: La Douane burkinabè a saisi le 23 juillet 2026, un car de transport en commun avec 60 millions de faux billets de F CFA, 5kg de drogue 99 plaquettes de TAPENTADOL, 360 plaquettes de VASILIUM, entre autres. Les Douaniers burkinabè ont, une fois de plus, démontrer leur détermination à lutter contre les actes frauduleux. Le 23 juillet 2026, ils ont saisi à Tenkodogo, dans la partie centre-est du Burkina Faso, un car de transport en commun qui transportait uniquement des marchandises diverses d’une valeur marché intérieur totale estimé à 75 604 350 francs cfa. Parmi les saisies, figure 60 millions de faux billets de francs cfa en coupures de 5000 F CFA, d’un poids total de 12 kilogrammes, 99 plaquettes de TAPENTADOL d’un poids total de trois kilogrammes d’une valeur marché interieur 2 044 350 francs cfa; 360 plaquettes de VASILIUM d’un poids total de dix kilogrammes d’une valeur 960 000 francs cfa; dix boules de chanvre indien d’un poids total de cinq kilogrammes d’une valeur 600 000 francs cfa. Le car saisi est quant à lui été évalué 10 000 000 francs cfa. Le propriétaire du véhicule qui a été interpellé dit ne pas être responsable des marchandises illicites saisies. Selon le Directeur général des Douanes, Dr Yves Kafando, il sera placé en garde-à-vue et présenté au procureur pour la suite de la procédure. Plus d'informations à venir… L’article Burkina: 60 millions FCFA de faux billets, 5kg de drogue et autres marchandises saisis est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Agou/Sécurité alimentaire : Un projet en faveur des agriculteurs lancé
items.description: Agou-Gadzépé, 13 août (ATOP) – L’association Nyanyuie a officiellement lancé, le mercredi 12 août à Amoussoukopé dans la commune Agou 2, le projet « Sécurité alimentaire durable pour les familles d’agriculteurs au Togo ». L’initiative de l’association Nyanyuie a bénéficié de l’appui financier du parlement et le ministère d’Etat du Baden-Württemberg via la Fondation pour la coopération au développement du Baden-Württemberg et de ANDA e.V. Elle a pour objectif de renforcer les compétences des producteurs en techniques agroécologiques, la préservation des sols, la production adaptée au climat, la conservation, la transformation et la commercialisation des produits agricoles. Le projet sera mis en œuvre sur une période de 12 mois (de juillet 2026 à juin 2027) dans dix villages de la commune. Plusieurs activités seront menées. Dix femmes et dix hommes de 18 à 35 ans, actifs dans l’agriculture seront formés. Par le mécanisme de transfert des connaissances, au moins 100 autres agriculteurs devraient aussi être touchés indirectement, avec un impact potentiel sur environ 700 personnes. L’assistance a suivi la présentation globale du projet. Elle a été également entretenue sur l’importance de l’agroécologie, le rôle des producteurs dans la réussite du projet et l’accompagnement technique prévu. Les participants ont échangé, en outre, avec les représentants des services techniques sur la transhumance et les effets du changement climatique. Le président de l’association Nyanyuie, Koto Komi Wolako a souhaité que les connaissances qui seront acquises par les producteurs soient mises en pratique. « Nous voulons voir des producteurs expérimenter de nouvelles techniques dans leurs parcelles, observer les résultats, identifier ce qui fonctionne, corriger ce qui ne fonctionne pas et partager leurs expériences avec leurs voisins », a dit M. Koto. Le maire de la commune Agou 2, Sakpa Koofi, a souligné que ce projet apporte des solutions concrètes aux défis que rencontrent les producteurs : baisse de fertilité des sols, pertes post-récoltes, difficultés d’accès aux marchés. Il a encouragé les bénéficiaires à saisir cette opportunité pour transformer durablement leurs pratiques agricoles, améliorer leurs revenus et renforcer la sécurité alimentaire de leurs familles. M. Sakpa a exprimé l’engagement de sa commune à accompagner ce projet en vue de sa réussite. ATOP/BSM/BV

items.title: Tône/Décentralisation : Le conseil régional fait le bilan du 1er semestre de mise en œuvre de son plan biennal 2026-2027
items.description: Dapaong, 13 août (ATOP) – Un atelier de revue semestrielle du plan d’actions biennal 2026-2027 du conseil régional des Savanes a réuni les acteurs impliqués, le mercredi 12 août à Dapaong. Cette assise a permis aux conseillers de dresser un bilan des six premiers mois de mise en œuvre afin d’ajuster les actions et maintenir la dynamique de développement au service des populations de la région. D’après le bilan, plusieurs activités prévues ont été réalisées dans les domaines de l’eau, l’éducation et la santé, ceci grâce à la mobilisation de tous les acteurs, notamment le conseil régional, les services déconcentrés de l’État, les partenaires techniques et financiers et la société civile. Il s’agit, entre autres, de la construction de forages à motricité humaine, des salles de classe et maternités dans certaines localités. La synergie entre les institutions a permis d’optimiser les ressources et d’éviter les doublons, garantissant ainsi une meilleure efficacité des interventions. Toutefois des difficultés ont été relevées dans l’exécution de certaines activités et la coordination entre les différents acteurs. Les participants ont aussi formulé des recommandations pour améliorer les performances au cours du prochain semestre. Pour le premier vice-président du conseil régional, Nambiema Daouda Wattara, le bilan est globalement positif et les résultats obtenus témoignent de la pertinence de la collaboration entre les acteurs et de la capacité collective à agir pour l’intérêt général. Validé le 3 février dernier, le tout premier plan d’actions biennal 2026-2027 est une feuille de route pour le développement régional. Il comprend quatre programmes, onze projets et cinquante-quatre activités, pour un budget total de 4 950 240 000 francs CFA, financé conjointement par la région et ses partenaires. Il vise à renforcer l’action du Conseil régional dans ses domaines de compétence et à améliorer les conditions de vie des populations. ATOP/JK/SED/BV

items.title: A Perfect Album for a Frustrating Decade
items.description: One of the coronavirus pandemic’s many terrible legacies is the slow smothering of ambition in popular culture. In the depths of the crisis, media—music, movies, and all the rest—were widely hailed as a “balm” for anxieties and a “lifeline” to the shared society we could look forward to someday returning to. Yet at the same time, that pre-pandemic sense of cohesion was being destabilized . Entertainers emerged from lockdown to find their fans wild-eyed with obsession and everyone else utterly unreachable. The ensuing years in the arts have felt strange and stilted —defined by stalled dreams, a shattered common stage, and a nervous relationship between artists and audiences. The Southern California folk singer Phoebe Bridgers is one artist who experienced the unique intensity of a pandemic breakthrough. In June of 2020, her hushed and biting second album, Punisher , was received with the sort of acclaim suggesting the arrival of the next great American songwriter. She was funny and thoughtful on social media, and fans came to regard her with all the intimacy of a best friend—despite her requests for them to step back and respect boundaries . Now, after more than half a decade, she’s released her third full-length album, Lost Weekend —a beautiful but frustrating document of post-pandemic disappointment. From her early days drawing buzz as a teenage disciple of pillow-voiced balladeers such as John Lennon and Elliott Smith, Bridgers’s appeal has lain in her ambivalence. She is an adventurer with a reclusive streak; she wants to see the world outside of her phone and then get back to bed. Many of her songs play like travelogues through a corrupted civilization—its skies littered with chemtrails and satellites, its bars patrolled by users and abusers. Her sighing style of singing and the downward lilt of her melodies suggest that the world’s fallen nature simply tires her out. “There’s no place like my room,” she sings on Punisher ’s closing track, “I Know the End.” In the years after that album, Bridgers didn’t actually disappear. She collaborated with the likes of Paul McCartney, SZA, and Taylor Swift, who proclaimed “she is the reference now” for modern songwriters. She released a splashy album with the supergroup boygenius . But none of this work had the sheer density of insight—the line-after-line sense of surprise—that has defined Bridgers’s solo music. (Her 2017 single “Motion Sickness” begins “I hate you for what you did / And I miss you like a little kid / I faked it every time, but that’s alright.”) Earlier this year, she embarked on a tour at which audience members were banned from using their phones—a sign that she was coming back to her main project on her own, self-protective terms. On paper, Lost Weekend is everything that the follow-up to a breakthrough should be: epic-scale, richly orchestrated, musically evolutionary. A glittering cast of collaborators includes the hitmaking producer Jack Antonoff, the Pulitzer-winning composer Caroline Shaw, the indie multi-instrumentalist Alex G, the mandolin-wielding MacArthur fellow Chris Thile, and— suspectedly , under a pseudonym—the It Boy vocalist of 2020s rock, Geese’s Cameron Winter . They’ve created a moody, varied soundscape featuring drum machines, hard guitars, and oases of country plucking. The first three songs are stunning. “The Outside” opens with Bridgers alternating between Laurie Anderson–style vocoder confessions and swirling piano paired with clean vocals. As she moves from the inorganic to the organic and back again, she also slips between tempos for an effect as mesmerizing as a shadow flickering in a stream. Then comes “Lost Boys,” a should-be smash single in which layers of chiming instruments coalesce into one swinging, shaggy mass. On “Kill Me,” rustling guitars convey cold unease until the chorus offers a hint of warmth. “This is gonna kill me,” sings Bridgers. Then she pauses to add, offbeat, “wait.” These early tracks portray Bridgers at the height of her success—crowd-surfing at concerts and surrounded by friends—yet feeling alienated. “I pretended it was make believe,” goes a great line from “Lost Boys,” capturing the psychological trickery that results from disassociating from one’s own life. When “Kill Me” crescendos in gang-sung cries of “Let’s go missing,” it’s an exciting cliff-hanger: Bridgers sounds poised to take the listener down a rabbit hole to somewhere fantastical and fresh. Instead, reality persists, murky and enervating. “The Governor’s Waltz” finds her at a famous music festival, feeling—yet again—disconnected and on edge. Fingerpicked guitars and toybox melodies are creepy yet obvious, like a Tim Burton movie. The lyrics bait gossip blogs by seeming to refer to an ex and the girl he replaced her with. These blind items should be interesting: Bridgers once knew how to make inside jokes land for everyone. But many of her descriptions, across the album, are naggingly opaque or inert. “You had a nosebleed, you were in my way / And you didn’t remind me of anything,” she sings, a line that’s intriguing only because it hints at her own creative blockage. [ Read: Decoding the most important songwriter of our time ] For much of the rest of the album, she seems to want to let her musicians do the talking. A number of songs are structurally fragmentary, featuring sudden cuts into silence or lengthy digressions into “folktronica” (a term for banjos-and-beats music of the sort that was last trendy in the 2000s). These seemingly avant-garde touches unfortunately scan more like boho-café fare. In May, Bridgers was seen wearing a T-shirt for Kid A —the numbed-out, synth-driven curveball that Radiohead released in 2000 after achieving alternative-rock dominance. But Bridgers isn’t leading a cutting-edge band that’s built up internal chemistry over years for unpredictable results. She’s enlisted a prestigious mishmash of stars to whip up variations on two moods: looming dread and wistful uplift. The story she’s telling should have been strong enough to land without so much filigree. On “Still Standing,” she seems to refer to abuse of her mother by her father, who died in late 2022. Rather than just condemning him, Bridgers spends part of the album examining the traits he passed on to her, for good and ill. At the same time, she’s wrestling with a fatalistic view of fame. “Surviving my gift until I get shot,” she sings on the title track—a chilling line on an album with a Lennon-inspired name . Her personal demons and public pressures really do sound suffocating. Can she possibly escape them? The twist of Lost Weekend is that it suggests a happy answer to that question. On the roaring and catchy “Bobby,” she sings about a blissful home life with a lover, who also shows up as a savior figure in other songs. Their meet-cute seems to be described in the first line: “I saw you slow dancing alone in your room.” Bobby is almost certainly her real boyfriend, the comedian Bo Burnham, and she’s implying that she fell for him while watching his acclaimed 2021 Netflix special, Bo Burnham: Inside , a document of stir-crazed social isolation. It’s quite the revelation: Back in the pandemic, Bridgers was in the exact same position as her audience—stuck at home and having her life changed by something on a screen. Burnham, himself an object of overwhelming public fascination, has mostly stayed out of the spotlight since Inside , though he has seven writing credits on this album . Virtual desire becoming real, isolation giving way to communion, a life built outside the digital panopticon—these are powerful themes for the 2020s. But too often, the album meets its moment in a sad way: with strained, distant songwriting that suggests its creator’s hesitation about reconnecting with the crowd.

items.title: Séisme en Colombie : 265 morts, 3 500 blessés et 500 disparus, les secours dans une course contre la montre
items.description: Trois jours après le puissant séisme qui a frappé l’ouest de la Colombie, les opérations de recherche entrent dans une phase critique. Les secours tentent toujours de retrouver des survivants sous les décombres, alors que le bilan s’élève désormais à 265 morts, près de 3 500 blessés et environ 500 disparus. Le tremblement de terre, dont l’épicentre se trouvait dans le département pauvre du Chocó, sur la côte Pacifique, a particulièrement touché plusieurs villes de l’ouest du pays, dont Cali et Pereira. Il s’agit du séisme le plus meurtrier enregistré en Colombie depuis le début du siècle. Alors que les recherches se poursuivent, les secours abordent désormais la fin de la période considérée comme la plus favorable à la survie des personnes coincées sous les décombres. Les premières 72 heures après un séisme sont en effet considérées comme particulièrement cruciales pour retrouver des survivants. Cette échéance doit arriver à son terme jeudi matin. « Nous entrons dans la phase finale des premières 72 heures », a déclaré le maire de Cali, Alejandro Eder, tout en rappelant que des survivants pouvaient encore être retrouvés au-delà de cette période, même si les chances diminuent. À Cali et Pereira, les équipes de secours se préparaient mercredi à passer une troisième nuit consécutive sur le terrain. Secouristes professionnels, bénévoles, chiens renifleurs et engins de levage sont mobilisés pour tenter de localiser les personnes toujours prisonnières des bâtiments effondrés. Pour les secouristes, chaque minute compte. Malgré les difficultés liées à l’ampleur des destructions, certains continuent de croire que des personnes peuvent encore être sauvées. Le bilan humain continue par ailleurs de s’alourdir. Selon les derniers chiffres communiqués par les autorités colombiennes, 265 personnes ont perdu la vie et près de 3 500 ont été blessées. Quelque 500 personnes sont toujours portées disparues. Les dégâts matériels sont également considérables. Plus de 11 000 logements ont été détruits, laissant des milliers de familles sans toit et compliquant davantage la prise en charge des populations touchées. Le nouveau président colombien, Abelardo de la Espriella, entré en fonction la semaine dernière, a annoncé trois jours de deuil national afin de rendre hommage aux victimes de cette catastrophe. Alors que les opérations de recherche se poursuivent, la Colombie entre donc dans une période particulièrement critique. À Cali, Pereira et dans les autres zones sinistrées, les secours continuent de fouiller les décombres, avec l'espoir de transformer les prochaines heures en nouvelles opérations de sauvetage. The post Séisme en Colombie : 265 morts, 3 500 blessés et 500 disparus, les secours dans une course contre la montre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Supercoupe d’Europe: un 2ème titre pour le Paris Saint-Germain
items.description: La Supercoupe d’Europe, une compétition opposant le vainqueur de la Ligue des Champions au vainqueur de la Ligue Europa de la saison sportive écoulée, s’est jouée mercredi 12 août 2026 à Salzbourg (Autriche). Elle a opposé le Paris Saint-Germain, double champion d’Europe aux Anglais d’Aston Villa, vainqueurs de la Ligue Europa. A l’arrivée, comme beaucoup d’observateurs et analystes sportifs avertis s’y attendaient, les Parisiens se sont imposés 2-1, pour le plus grand bonheur de leurs dirigeants et supporters. Ils s’offrent ainsi un deuxième titre dans cette compétition. L’année dernière, l’on s’en souvient, ils ont remporté leur premier titre en Supercoupe d’Europe aux dépens d’un autre club anglais (Tottenham). La saison dernière, la formation d’Aston Villa avait pourtant montré de bonnes choses en Premier League et sur la scène européenne. Le club phare de Birmingham a remporté, 44 ans après son sacre en C1 (actuelle Ligue des Champions de l’UEFA), son deuxième trophée dans les compétitions européennes de football. Une victoire historique à mettre évidemment à l’actif de son entraîneur espagnol Unai Emery, qui totalise désormais 5 titres en Ligue Europa (3 avec le FC Séville, 1 avec Villarreal et 1 avec Aston Villa). A noter que le Real Madrid, avec ses 6 titres, est le club le plus capé en Supercoupe d’Europe. Le club madrilène est suivi de son grand rival, le FC Barcelone (5 titres), de l’AC Milan (5 titres), de Liverpool FC (4 titres) et de l’Atlético de Madrid (3 titres). Les clubs ayant remporté deux fois la compétition sont : Bayern Munich, Chelsea, Juventus, Anderlecht, Valence, Ajax Amsterdam. Le Paris Saint-Germain vient de rejoindre ce club des doubles vainqueurs de la Supercoupe d’Europe. Almamy Samadou L’article Supercoupe d’Europe: un 2ème titre pour le Paris Saint-Germain est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Tône/Crise sécuritaire dans les Savanes : Une formation pratique pour soutenir les jeunes et les femmes
items.description: Dapaong, 13 août (ATOP) – Un atelier de formation pratique destiné à renforcer les capacités des personnes ressources accompagnant les jeunes et les femmes vulnérables de la région des Savanes s’est tenu les 11 et 12 août à Dapaong. La formation est initiée par Plan international Togo, bureau régional des Savanes et de la Kara, dans le cadre du projet « Action intégrée de réponse de crise dans la région des Savanes (Savanes Kpaadu) ». Ce projet est mis en œuvre en partenariat avec les ONG Communication pour un développement durable (CDD), Humanité & inclusion (Handicap International) et la Centrale africaine pour un développement intégral et durable (CADID). L’objectif est de renforcer les capacités des personnes ressources pour les rendre capables d’accompagner les bénéficiaires dans l’élaboration de plans d’affaires viables, favorisant ainsi la création d’Activités génératrices de revenus (AGR) et l’autonomisation économique. Une séquence de la formation L’atelier a réuni 40 personnes ressources de 10 communes des préfectures de Tône, Cinkassé, Kpendjal et Kpendjal ouest, ainsi que des représentants de Plan International Togo et des partenaires locaux. Les participants ont bénéficié de modules interactifs sur la structuration d’un plan d’affaires, les critères de sélection des bénéficiaires, les mécanismes de recours et la gestion des plaintes. Des exercices pratiques, des études de cas et des simulations ont permis d’ancrer les acquis. Pour les organisateurs, ce projet est initié pour faire face aux problèmes de l’afflux de plus de 49 000 réfugiés et 10 000 déplacés internes, dont une majorité d’enfants, dans la région des Savanes. Ce déplacement massif entraine des défis majeurs en matière de sécurité, d’accès aux services sociaux de base et de développement économique. Ce projet a vu le jour pour renforcer la cohésion sociale, la protection civile et la résilience économique des populations Les participants ont exprimé leur gratitude à Plan international et ses partenaires pour cette formation qui leur a permis d’être assez outillés pour accompagner les jeunes et femmes de la région dans la création et la gestion de leurs projets économiques, contribuant ainsi à renforcer la résilience des communautés face à la crise. La même formation est prévue les 14 et 15 août à Mango au profit de 24 personnes ressources de 6 communes des préfectures de Tandjouaré, Oti et Oti sud. ATOP/TKA/JK/SED
